items.title: 52222_Marshall Royal oral history interview
items.q: my band, which my rhythm section was the King Cole Trio

ctx.x: originally played, after Cee Pee C.P. Johnson's band left out of there. See, Cee Pee C.P. lost half his band when Lionel Hampton formed his band because I went with Lionel Hampton. My brother was the trumpet player. He went with Lionel Hampton and my -- the baritone saxophone player was Jack MacVeigh, the guy that wrote the tune, "Open the Door, Richard." He went with the Lionel Hampton Orchestra, so that sort of messed up that band by taking half of them and as a matter of fact, Lionel was so forward, he…

Oh, he was sort of in with it. So really, what gave him the idea of that was the fact that in the year 1939, Labor Day, they had a great big parade which was always the thing in California of having the Labor Day Parade. On this particular Labor Day, two big bands were in town. It was the Count Basie Band and the Jimmie Lunceford Band. So, we had always had a walking band that represented local 767, the black local of Los Angeles. So, this time, I was vice president of the local, and I suggested to the board of…
